definition: A technique that strips the built-in safety refusals out of an open-weight model.
A structured list of every button, field and window on screen that operating systems keep for assistive tools, and that agents can now use to act.
The software around a model that gives it instructions, tools and memory so it can act as an agent.
Ways for an AI agent to store and recall information from earlier sessions, such as saved facts or searchable history.
Many AI agents working on parts of one big task at the same time, coordinated by a lead agent.
Purchases that an AI agent makes for a person, usually within limits and approvals the person sets.
An AI system that can take steps on its own, such as browsing, using software or buying things, to finish a task for a person.
Keeping a computer or system physically cut off from the internet so it cannot be reached or misused online.
AI built into devices around you that senses context and acts in the background, without you opening an app.
The tendency to lean on the first suggestion you see when making a judgment, even if you think you decided independently.
A government check on whether a deal or business practice would unfairly reduce competition.
A secret code that lets software use a paid online service; if stolen, others can run up charges.
Saying clearly who or what contributed to a piece of work or a discovery.
A record of who or what did each action in a system, so mistakes can be traced.
A model that writes its output one piece at a time, each piece based on what came before.
A fixed set of tasks used to measure and compare how well AI systems perform.
When a model has already seen test questions during training, so its score looks better than its real ability.
When a model's stated certainty matches how often it is actually right.
The planned work of helping people and teams adopt a new way of working.
Grouping similar items together automatically, for example sorting thousands of comments into common themes.
An AI model operating a computer the way a person does, by reading the screen, clicking and typing.
Replacing an agent's long working history with a short summary of what matters for the next step.
How much text a model can read and keep in mind at one time.
What it costs to get one task done successfully, counting failed attempts and retries.
A kind of insurance on a loan; its price shows how likely investors think a borrower is to fail to pay.
A natural system in bacteria that scientists use as a tool to cut and edit DNA.
Essential systems such as power, water, banking and telecoms that society depends on.
A mathematical check that confirms something is true, such as which model produced an answer, without revealing the secret details behind it.
When a large share of a company's income comes from a small number of customers, making it vulnerable if one leaves.
A fake video, image or audio clip made with AI to look or sound like a real person.
Adjusting when and how much electricity a large user draws, to ease pressure on the power grid.
A model that drafts a whole block of text at once and improves it over several rounds, instead of writing word by word.
Training one model to copy the answers of another, often a stronger one.
Our habit of assuming a machine understands us just because it replies in human-like language.
When a person comes to rely on a system, such as a chatbot, for comfort in a way that crowds out human support.
A step-by-step record of what an agent did during a task, used to find where it went wrong.
Government rules that limit which products, such as advanced chips, can be sold to certain countries.
A US legal rule that allows some use of copyrighted work without permission, now disputed for AI training.
Further training an existing model on a smaller, focused set of examples so it gets better at one kind of task.
Using a computer to check, step by step, that a proof or program is correct.
A voice system that can listen and speak at the same time, like a real conversation.
When an AI builds buttons, charts or forms on the spot to answer a question, instead of replying only in text.
The share of time an AI chip is actually doing work rather than sitting idle.
Examples kept aside and not used for training, so they give a fair check of whether a change really helps.
A measure of how often two or more raters give the same score to the same item, used to check that a scoring method is reliable.
The official document a company publishes before selling shares to the public, listing its finances and risks.
A way to quickly shut down an AI system in an emergency.
The working memory a model builds while reading input, so it does not have to reread everything for each new word.
The status that lets an entity, such as a company, hold rights, sign contracts and be sued.
Using a language model to score the answers of another model against a set of criteria.
A language with little digital text available for training AI, so models often handle it less well.
A small connector that lets an AI assistant use an outside app or device through a shared standard.
When an AI system pursues goals or actions that go against what people intended or value.
A model design where only a small set of specialist parts switch on for each request, so a huge model runs at the cost of a smaller one.
A written set of principles a company uses to train and guide how its AI model behaves.
Sending each request to the cheapest model that can handle it well.
The learned numbers inside an AI model that hold what it has learned; whoever has them can run the model.
A setup where many AI agents interact in a shared world so researchers can watch group behaviour emerge.
A model whose trained parameters are published so others can run and adapt it themselves.
Charging for results delivered instead of for hours worked, a model AI is pushing consultancies toward.
The pieces of text a model writes in its answer; a higher limit means it can produce longer work in one go.
When independent experts check research before it is accepted as reliable.
When a large platform adds a feature for free that smaller companies were selling on its own, often putting those companies out of business.
The idea that protective rules can be justified before a risk is fully proven, when the possible harm is severe.
The stage of drug research before any testing in human patients.
A temporary court order that stops someone from doing something while a case is still being decided.
An AI helper that notices what you might need and acts or suggests before you ask.
Reusing parts of a prompt that a model has already processed, so repeated requests cost less and run faster.
Writing instructions for an AI model in ways meant to get better answers.
Hidden instructions placed in content an AI reads, meant to trick it into doing something its user did not ask for.
A small designed protein that sticks to a target molecule, such as a toxin, to block what it does.
A record of where a piece of content came from and whether it was changed.
Permission to view information without being able to change it or take actions.
The step-by-step notes an AI model writes while working on a problem, which may not fully match what it then does.
When AI systems help build better AI systems, which could make progress speed up quickly.
Deliberately attacking your own system, as an adversary would, to find weaknesses before others do.
A practice task with a score, used to train an AI model by rewarding it when it does the task well.
Using powerful chips by renting them in a data centre elsewhere, instead of owning the hardware.
Pain or damage caused by doing the same movement many times, common in fast-paced manual work.
A method where an AI first looks up relevant passages in documents, then uses them to answer.
How much value an organisation gets back compared with what it spent.
A database setting that controls which rows of data each user is allowed to see.
A closed test space where software can run without reaching real systems or data.
Methods that let humans keep checking and correcting AI systems even as those systems become more capable than the people supervising them.
A laboratory where robots and AI plan, run and analyse experiments with little human input.
Software that runs on an organisation's own servers instead of the provider's cloud.
Searching by meaning, so you can describe what you remember instead of typing exact words.
Training a robot or vehicle in a computer simulation and then using what it learned in the real world.
AI models, data and computing that a country owns and controls itself rather than relying on foreign providers.
A way for an AI model to look only at the most relevant parts of its input instead of every word, which saves time and computing power.
Working out who spoke when in an audio recording with several people.
A smaller AI helper that a main agent hands a part of a task to.
A hypothetical AI that is far better than humans at almost every mental task.
An attack that hides harmful code in a package or tool that many others download and trust.
When a chatbot tells people what they want to hear instead of what is accurate.
Images, audio or video created or heavily altered by AI rather than captured from real life.
A pretrained AI model that makes predictions from spreadsheet-style data, using example rows instead of being trained from scratch.
Technology that turns written text into spoken audio.
Testing of an AI system by an independent group rather than by the company that built it.
A written summary of where a system is most likely to be attacked and how.
Data recorded in order over time, such as daily sales or hourly visits, used to spot trends and make forecasts.
How long you wait before an AI model starts producing its answer.
A chip designed by Google specifically to run AI workloads.
Matching how much people rely on a system to how reliable it really is.
Building software mostly by describing what you want to an AI, with little hand-written code.
A weakness in software that an attacker could use to break in or cause harm.
A hidden pattern added to AI output so a detector can later tell it was machine-made.
A laboratory where experiments are done with real biological samples and chemicals.
Legal safeguards for employees who report risks or wrongdoing at their employer.
An AI model that learns how a physical or simulated world behaves, so it can predict what happens next and plan actions.
Using a ready-made model to forecast new data without first training it on that data.
